repo-multimodal-fusion-covid-19-code.summary: A research codebase for COVID-19 diagnosis experiments that fuse clinical and imaging data across three experimental scenarios. Its dataset balancing utilities use SDV's SingleTableMetadata and GaussianCopulaSynthesizer/CTGANSynthesizer to generate synthetic minority-class samples for class imbalance correction.

repo-vae-record-generator.summary: A variational autoencoder for tabular data generation, written from scratch to capture the distribution of a record set and sample from it. Its categorical encoding is RDT's: `utils/_transformer.py` imports `OneHotEncodingTransformer` from `rdt.transformers`, with `rdt==0.5.0` in the requirements though commented out. RDT's transformer is called as the encoding layer of an independently written VAE.

repo-cd-linter-artifacts.summary: The replication package for 'Configuration Smells in Continuous Delivery Pipelines', carrying the mined GitLab CI configuration files and linter results the study is based on. The only matches for `sdv` in the whole archive are substrings inside base64 CSRF tokens and certificate blobs in captured HTML — `dsdvkq`, `EsdVne`. Recorded at importance 0 so this substring accident is not re-examined.

repo-gans-genomics.summary: Applies CTGAN to genomic tabular data, carrying the synthesizer source in-tree.

repo-machine-learning-study.summary: A personal set of Chinese-language machine-learning study notes with accompanying code, organised by topic. The data-processing module runs both paths of the SDV family: `sdv.tabular.GaussianCopula` with `sdv.evaluation` for scoring, and `CTGANSynthesizer` imported directly. The pre-1.0 namespace dates the material.

repo-fingerprinting-toolbox.summary: A library for embedding and extracting ownership fingerprints in relational data, with a robustness suite that attacks fingerprinted copies of the German Credit, Nursery and Breast Cancer datasets. SDV appears only as a schema utility: the attack scripts call `SingleTableMetadata().detect_from_dataframe` on each fingerprinted table, and `sdv==1.3.0`, `ctgan==0.7.4` and `sdmetrics==0.11.0` are pinned. SDV's metadata layer is run for schema detection; no synthesizer or metric is used.

repo-dsinvariant.summary: An OCaml tool for inferring data-structure invariants, composing verifiers, synthesizers and learners through a functor interface. The pooled match is a name collision: `App.ml` instantiates its pipeline with `ParSynthesizer.T`, a parallel-search synthesizer module of its own, whose name contains `PARSynthesizer` as a substring. There is no Python, no dependency and nothing to do with SDV's sequential model.

repo-rdt.summary: Reversible Data Transforms: the preprocessing layer that converts arbitrary column types into numeric form for modeling and inverts the transformation afterwards, including anonymization transformers such as AnonymizedFaker and RegexGenerator.

docs-bundle-cag.summary: Add-on that applies complex business logic across multiple tables during generation, auto-detects constraints from data, and supports programmable constraints beyond the predefined set.

docs-bundle-xsynthesizers.summary: Enhanced models and transformers: XGC (flexible-shape copula modeling), SegmentSynthesizer for highly segmented data, BootstrapSynthesizer for very small tables, plus ECDF and 100+ distribution normalizers.

paper-bayesian-multi-model-inference-202.summary: This paper proposes a Bayesian multi-model inference framework to address epistemic uncertainty in vine copula structure selection for structural reliability analysis under limited data, using Bayes factors to reweight candidate vine structures and integrating this with a first-order reliability method for regular vine copulas. It is a methods paper in structural/civil engineering reliability analysis, illustrated with numerical and engineering examples. The SDV-family paper on learning vine copula models for synthetic data generation (Sun, Cuesta-Infante, Veeramachaneni 2019) is cited only in the reference list as prior vine-copula literature, with no visible engagement or reuse of its method in the body text shown.

paper-systematic-literature-review-gener.summary: This is a systematic literature review, following PRISMA guidelines, surveying generative AI approaches (GANs, VAEs, diffusion models, transformer architectures) for producing synthetic clinical data across EHRs, imaging, genomics, time series, and text, assessing the tradeoff between data realism and patient privacy. It synthesizes findings from studies published 2018-2024 and highlights gaps in rigorous re-identification risk evaluation. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GAN capability in capturing complex clinical data distributions, without further engagement or experimentation.

paper-tea-cgan-framework-mitigating-2026.summary: This paper proposes TEA-CGAN, a conditional GAN-based framework designed to mitigate class imbalance in disease risk prediction by synthesizing samples for underrepresented classes. The work situates itself among GAN-based oversampling approaches used to balance class distributions in medical/health data. CTGAN is cited only in passing, alongside other GAN literature, as prior work using adversarial training to synthesize minority-class samples.

paper-ctgan-autoencoder-conditional-tabu.summary: This paper proposes a framework that couples an autoencoder, used for dimensionality reduction and latent feature extraction across multi-omics cancer data, with a Conditional Tabular GAN that generates synthetic minority-class samples to correct severe class imbalance before training a neural network to predict bladder-cancer TMB and breast-cancer menopausal status. The empirical pipeline's synthetic-sample generation stage rests on CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, run to oversample underrepresented classes in the multi-omics datasets.

paper-adapted-gan-models-efficiently-202.summary: This paper benchmarks GAN-based tabular synthesizers (CTGAN, CopulaGAN) adapted for multi-sequence data against the sequential model CPAR to generate privacy-preserving synthetic longitudinal prostate-cancer biomarker records, evaluating fidelity, predictive utility, privacy risk, and computational efficiency on a dataset of nearly 20,000 patients. The entire empirical programme runs SDV-ecosystem synthesizers directly: CTGAN and CopulaGAN (with their mode-specific normalization and Gaussian-copula components, via RDT for transforms) and CPAR/Sequential SDV as evaluation subjects, with fidelity and disclosure metrics computed via SDMetrics' Column Shape/Pair Trend scores and Disclosure Protection Estimate. SDV's CTGAN, CopulaGAN, and CPAR synthesizers are run as the generators under comparison, forming the entire empirical results of the paper.

paper-conditional-distribution-estimatio.summary: This paper proposes a tabular diffusion-based framework (built on TabDDPM) for generating and imputing residential building characteristics to fill data gaps in urban building energy models, trained on a 2.2-million-building ResStock dataset and validated with a Baltimore case study. In its related-work discussion of generative approaches to tabular data, the paper cites CTGAN, along with other GAN- and VAE-based tabular methods, as prior work with 'suboptimal generation quality' that motivates its diffusion-based approach. CTGAN is only cited as prior art the authors depart from, not run or benchmarked in experiments.

paper-credit-risk-modeling-unsupervised-.summary: This paper proposes improving a bank's corporate credit risk model by representing small and medium enterprises as nodes and their money transfers as weighted edges in a graph, then using unsupervised GraphSAGE to learn node representations that feed into downstream risk prediction. In its literature review it describes several prior graph-based approaches to credit and fraud modeling, including a cited work that uses CTGAN to generate synthetic data points to reduce class imbalance in credit scoring datasets. CTGAN is only mentioned in passing as the method another cited paper used for class-imbalance mitigation, and is not run or engaged with by the authors' own work.

paper-effect-uncertainty-calibrated-chlo.summary: This paper reframes deterministic service-life prediction of reinforced concrete infrastructure as a decision-risk problem, using machine-learning models to infer chloride diffusion coefficients from experimental datasets and propagating the resulting uncertainty through corrosion initiation and life-cycle maintenance models. It quantifies how this uncertainty shifts maintenance demand, emissions, and costs relative to deterministic estimates. CTGAN is cited as an SDV-family reference, with no indication from the available evidence of how or whether it was actually run.
paper-effect-uncertainty-calibrated-chlo.needs: Full text needed to determine whether CTGAN was used for data augmentation/synthesis of experimental datasets or merely cited in passing among ML methods.

paper-exhaustive-structure-learning-vine.summary: This paper develops a flexible density-estimation framework for multiband LTE/5G spectrum resource-block utilization using Regular vine (R-vine) copulas, performing an exhaustive search over admissible vine structures with Gaussian Mixture Copula pair-copula terms and validating the approach on real LTE measurement data. The only SDV-family reference found is citation [15], described as formulating vine structure learning as a sequential reinforcement-learning decision problem, which does not match the SDV/copulas package's own methodology or any run of its code. No SDV-family term or usage appears anywhere in the extracted full text, suggesting the citation match is a mismatch between an unrelated vine-copula paper and the indexed SDV vine-copula reference.

paper-fuzzy-distribution-modeling-synthe.summary: This paper proposes a fuzzy-set-based methodology for synthetic tabular data generation that represents feature distributions as fuzzy concepts and models dependencies via Fuzzy Cognitive Maps, aiming for interpretable, low-parameter data synthesis with causal structure preservation. It evaluates the approach on three health-related benchmark datasets against utility, fidelity, and privacy metrics. The proposed method is benchmarked against three synthesizers from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) framework -- Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE -- run with their default SDV configurations as comparison baselines.

paper-mitigating-non-iid-challenges-2026.summary: This paper proposes FL_nonIID_Synth, a federated learning protocol that augments each hospital client's local dataset with synthetic data to counter non-IID class and feature skew in horizontally partitioned medical datasets (diabetes and heart disease). The authors benchmark three synthetic data generators—DataSynthesizer, SDV, and Synthpop—on generation speed, correlation-matrix fidelity, and KL divergence, ultimately selecting Synthpop as the best-performing method for their FL framework. SDV is run as one of three evaluated synthetic-data generation methods and is found to be the slowest and to have higher KL divergence than the chosen alternative, so it is used but not adopted.

paper-physics-guided-augmentation-nonlin.summary: This paper proposes NSRL-PCGAN, a framework combining a physics-constrained GAN for generating mechanistically valid synthetic features with a nonlinear supervised representation learning encoder that assigns high-fidelity pseudo-labels, aimed at augmenting scarce labeled data for surface-roughness prediction in machining. It is validated on a self-built grinding dataset and a public milling dataset, showing notable RMSE reductions under limited-sample conditions. CTGAN is cited in the introduction as an example of a tabular-data GAN that jointly models discrete and continuous features for industrial data augmentation, but it is not run or built upon in the proposed method.
paper-physics-guided-augmentation-nonlin.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run as an experimental baseline or only cited in related work discussion.

paper-rare-but-critical-copula-2026.summary: A method paper proposing a copula-calibrated data augmentation approach to address imbalance in tabular regression tasks, aiming to better represent rare but important target values. The available evidence gives no further detail on the technical approach or experiments. It cites both the CTGAN (NeurIPS 2019) and SDV (DSAA 2016) papers, apparently as related prior work on synthetic tabular data generation.
paper-rare-but-critical-copula-2026.needs: Full text and abstract were not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN/SDV are run as baselines, adapted, or merely cited in related work. Title suggests a copula-based method distinct from SDV's GaussianCopula, but this cannot be verified.

paper-tabloft-tabular-generation-llm-202.summary: TabLoft is a large-language-model-based tabular data synthesis method that orders features according to a tree-model-informed strategy before fine-tuning the LLM, aiming to overcome the unidirectional information flow of transformer generation. The authors introduce five evaluation metrics and show state-of-the-art performance against six baseline generators including GReaT, PredLLM, TabDDPM and TabSYN. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of these six baseline models across MLE, authenticity, diversity, privacy and indistinguishability comparisons, with SDV's conditional-generator design for CTGAN described in the related work.
paper-tabloft-tabular-generation-llm-202.needs: The formally OpenAlex-detected SDV citation is the 2016 SDV/DSAA paper, appearing only in the reference list, while the CTGAN/TVAE baselines cited in-body are attributed to a separate reference [16] (likely Xu et al. 2019); it is unclear whether an sdv-dev package or an independent reimplementation was used to run these baselines.

paper-gan-software-fault-prediction-2025.summary: Compares five GAN variants, CopulaGAN, VanillaGAN, CTGAN, TGAN and WGANGP, as oversampling methods for software fault prediction, pairing each with Recursive Feature Elimination for feature selection and separately with autoencoders for feature extraction, then training six classifiers (Random Forest, XGBoost, HistGradientBoosting, MLP, Extra Trees, AdaBoost) on five PROMISE defect datasets (CM1, KC1, KC2, PC1, JM1) and scoring precision, recall, F1, AUC and MCC, with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test against SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and random undersampling. The conclusion is that the GAN oversamplers beat the interpolation-based baselines and that CTGAN is the best performer, followed by WGANGP and VanillaGAN, with the RFE plus CTGAN and autoencoder plus CTGAN pairings strongest across datasets. The paper is in the index because two of the five generators it runs are SDV synthesizers and it says so outright: CopulaGAN is described as a variation of CTGAN presented in the SDV open source library, with the SDV documentation page for the CopulaGAN synthesizer given as the reference, and its data preparation is attributed to Reversible Data Transformation. The CTGAN and CopulaGAN hyperparameter tables list embedding dim, generator dim, discriminator dim, generator lr, generator decay, discriminator lr and discriminator decay at their package defaults, which are the CTGANSynthesizer constructor arguments, so the sdv-dev package was run rather than an independent reimplementation. TGAN is credited to Xu and Veeramachaneni's earlier tabular GAN, and CTGAN's mode-specific normalization by variational Gaussian mixture and its conditional generator with training-by-sampling are reproduced in the method section.

paper-efficient-multi-institution-collab.summary: This paper proposes a collaborative learning framework for multi-institution credit risk assessment that avoids raw data sharing by having each institution generate synthetic data locally, filter it via a DBSCAN-based algorithm, and share only the filtered pseudo-dataset for phased fusion with other institutions' local data. Experiments on credit datasets show accuracy and recall gains after data fusion under both iid and non-iid settings. CTGAN is trained by each institution as the generator that produces the synthetic data underlying the whole pipeline, leveraging its conditional vector to address class imbalance in default/non-default samples.

paper-water-systems-gan-review-2025.summary: Reviews generative approaches for water distribution system data, where operators withhold records for security and legal reasons and researchers are left without a corpus. CTGAN is among the models found effective, so the review positions SDV as a route around a data-access problem that is institutional rather than technical.

paper-street-vendor-cgan-fintech-2025.summary: Surveys 1000 street vendors across three cities in Odisha and trains a small fairness-aware conditional GAN on nine socio-demographic and behavioural attributes, on the argument that informal-sector records are too few and too irregular for the credit-risk and fraud models that formal finance runs on. The generator is a three-layer MLP with fairness-aware loss reweighting rather than any existing tabular architecture, and the paper reports Frechet distance 10.12, behavioural entropy 3.59 bits, gains of 3.2 and 2.9 percent on loan-default prediction and anomaly detection from hybrid real-plus-synthetic training, and demographic-parity deviation held under 2.4 percent by audits every 50 epochs. CTGAN is the closest prior adversarial baseline and is trained and sampled on the same preprocessed dataset with aligned normalization and conditional inputs, losing to the proposed model on every reported measure. It appears only in that comparison role, so the entry records CTGAN as the benchmark a new generator is measured against.

paper-dp-netddpm-traffic-2025.summary: Proposes DP-NetDDPM, which applies a tabular denoising diffusion model to adversarial network packet generation under differential privacy, on the argument that diffusion captures packet-format structure and distribution better than the GAN and autoencoder synthesisers previously used for intrusion-detection data. TVAE, released alongside CTGAN, is one of the three synthesisers it is measured against on t-SNE distribution alignment, fidelity and machine-learning adaptability; CTGAN itself is named in the related-work account of GAN approaches to mixed types and imbalance but is not among the models run.

paper-arf-mortality-mimic-2025.summary: Builds a mortality predictor for acute respiratory failure that is deliberately cheap to train and deploy, drawing cohorts from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV and testing whether class rebalancing by synthetic generation improves sensitivity, the metric that matters when a false negative is a missed death. All three generators used are SDV synthesizers run from the library: CTGAN, CopulaGAN and TVAE each produce balanced training sets at fixed class ratios, and the reported sensitivity gains across the classifiers rest on their output.

paper-ensuring-quality-synthetic-used-20.summary: This conference paper proposes a topological-data-analysis method, based on Vietoris-Rips complexes and persistent homology, to improve the correlation fidelity of synthetic tabular data used for network intrusion detection. The authors generate synthetic network-intrusion data with CT-GAN and a VAE, then apply their TDA-based measure to make the generated data spaces topologically congruent to the original data. CT-GAN (citing the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper) is imported from a GitHub repository and run as one of two synthetic-data generators whose output is post-processed and evaluated by the proposed method.

paper-generating-heterogeneous-multi-dim.summary: This conference paper compares six data-generation methods -- random sampling, TVAE, a standard GAN, a conditional tabular GAN, and two diffusion models -- for producing synthetic firefighter-intervention records used in resource-allocation simulations. It evaluates the methods with standard metrics (precision, recall, density, coverage, Wasserstein distance, MMD) plus domain-specific criteria such as response-time and spatial-temporal distributions, finding diffusion models outperform the others while CTGAN and TVAE struggle with rare events and scalability. CTGAN and TVAE, both associated with the SDV/CTGAN paper, are run as two of the several generation models evaluated in the comparison.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-dy.summary: This is a survey paper that reviews and categorizes GAN-based approaches for generating and detecting dynamic malware behavior, addressing the challenges of applying GANs to tabular and sequential data with heavy-tailed, multimodal distributions. It surveys reviewed articles' use of models such as DCGAN, WGAN, SeqGAN, and CopulaGAN, and repeatedly invokes CTGAN's finding that tabular data exhibit multimodal distributions requiring mode-specific normalization to avoid mode collapse. CTGAN and CopulaGAN (the SDV package's models) are discussed and cited as prior art used by other reviewed works, but neither is run by the authors themselves.

paper-generative-artificial-intelligence.summary: This paper proposes VAE-BGM, a Variational AutoEncoder with Bayesian Gaussian Mixture, to augment mixed-type crash-severity data and address severe class imbalance, integrating traditional crash variables with adjacent vehicle detector data and evaluating via ROC-AUC. It reports that VAE-BGM outperforms other data augmentation methods, with baselines achieving 0.707-0.784 versus 0.813 for VAE-BGM. CTGAN and TVAE, both described via their SDV-family origin paper, are discussed and appear among the comparison augmentation methods against which the proposed generator is benchmarked.

paper-population-synthesis-incomplete-mi.summary: This paper proposes a WGAN-GP-based population synthesis method that trains on incomplete microsamples using a mask matrix to handle missing attribute values, validated against a Swedish national travel survey. The authors compare synthetic populations from models trained on incomplete versus complete microsamples and show close resemblance to the true population distribution. CTGAN is cited and discussed in related work as a promising conditional-generator approach for tabular data, and flagged as a future research avenue for conditioning on marginals, but it is not implemented or run in the study.

paper-internet-things-iot-intrusion-2025.summary: This paper proposes FS-TGAN, a feature-selection-based approach combined with Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks to address class imbalance in IoT network intrusion detection, evaluated on the UNSW-NB15 and NSL-KDD datasets. The authors use TGAN to synthesize minority-class malicious traffic samples, reporting 99.03% accuracy on UNSW-NB15 after data augmentation. TGAN, the tabular GAN component of the SDV family, is run as the core generator underpinning the entire empirical study, while CTGAN is only mentioned as a proposed future extension.

paper-copula-transferable-models-synthet.summary: This paper proposes copula-based models for generating synthetic populations that can be transferred across geographic contexts, targeting applications in transportation demand modeling. The authors discuss deep generative alternatives from the tabular-data literature, describing CTGAN and TVAE as GAN/VAE adaptations designed to handle mixed discrete and multimodal continuous columns. CTGAN and TVAE (from Xu et al.) are cited and their mechanics described as prior art in the related work discussion, without clear evidence from the abstract/citing sentences that they were run as experimental baselines.

paper-enhancing-clothing-size-prediction.summary: This paper evaluates several machine learning models -- Logistic Regression, KNN, Random Forest, and Decision Tree -- for predicting clothing size in e-commerce to reduce returns caused by poor fit. The best models (Random Forest and Decision Tree) achieve accuracy up to 0.99 for shirt size and up to 0.89 for pant size prediction. TGAN is mentioned only in passing in the related-work discussion as prior work on generating tabular data, and is not used in the study.

The work is unrelated to synthetic data generation; CTGAN is only named in a passing background sentence about generative methods used for financial data generation, listed alongside other GAN and autoencoder citations. CTGAN is cited only bibliographically, as one of several generative-model references, and is never run or discussed further in the text.

paper-enhancing-tabular-generation-knowl.summary: This paper proposes a large language model fine-tuning approach for generating high-quality tabular data in the aviation domain, combining LLM fine-tuning with an external knowledge base to improve table comprehension and generation accuracy. Experiments show a 22% improvement over a baseline LLM in generating tabular flight data. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited only in the reference list among prior tabular-data-generation works, with no evidence it was run.

paper-dual-ensemble-ids-ctgan-2024.summary: Attacks the class imbalance in UNSW-NB15, where intrusion records are far fewer than normal traffic and models trained on the raw set skew toward the majority class, with a two-stage label-wise stacking ensemble. Three deliberately weak binary classifiers, a decision tree, logistic regression and Gaussian naive Bayes, are trained per attack label on both the original and a balanced copy of the data; the best model per label feeds nine per-label XGBoost models, and a final XGBoost meta-classifier sits on top, reaching 98 percent accuracy on binary and 95 percent on multi-class classification, against the 93.88 percent binary and 80.96 percent multi-class figures of the ensemble study whose Chi-square feature selection the authors reuse for comparability. The balancing step generates CTGAN samples for every attack category up to 93,000 rows, matching the count of normal traffic, and the paper gives CTGAN its own methods section covering mode-specific normalisation via the variational Gaussian mixture model, the conditional vector and training-by-sampling, and the Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty objective. Decision-tree and naive-Bayes base classifiers improve on nearly every attack label once the data is balanced while logistic regression proves largely insensitive to imbalance, and the authors read the reduced false-positive count as the practically important gain for an intrusion detection system. The entry records CTGAN as the generator of every synthetic row in the study, named in the paper's title and presented as its main contribution to the literature.

paper-exploring-augmentation-active-lear.summary: This paper studies how to combine active learning with data augmentation to improve minority-class performance on imbalanced tabular datasets (Wine, Baseball, Steel Plates), comparing random oversampling, G-SMOTE, and CTGAN-based augmentation (including a per-class CTGAN variant) across active-learning query strategies. The authors report that CTGAN-based augmentation yields the largest gains for minority classes, sometimes near 50% improvement, and combine it with active learning to reduce labeled-data needs. CTGAN, from the SDV ecosystem, is run as one of several data-augmentation generators, with its own hyperparameter grid search (generator/discriminator dimensions, learning rates) and training curves reported in an appendix.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-cr.summary: This paper develops a conditional GAN (cGAN) architecture -- with an encoder, decoder, and discriminator -- to generate synthetic motion-capture data (marker trajectories, joint angles, and 3D ground reaction forces) conditioned on subject and gait characteristics such as age, sex, leg length, mass, and walking speed. The models are trained and validated against experimental gait datasets to show they can replicate and extrapolate kinematic and force patterns for biomechanics research. The CTGAN paper is cited among related generative-modeling work but is not run or adopted as a component of the proposed pipeline based on the available evidence.

paper-generative-models-synthetic-genera.summary: This paper benchmarks several deep-learning generative methods -- an MLP conditional GAN, TimeGAN, and the Probabilistic Autoregressive (PAR) model -- for producing synthetic patient covariate and PK/PD endpoint data, evaluating them with discriminative/predictive scores and statistical distribution tests. The authors describe PAR's two-stage architecture (a Gaussian copula for static covariates followed by an RNN for temporal data) in detail as one of the three benchmarked generators, finding the MLP cGAN performed best overall. SDV's PAR sequential synthesizer is run (or closely reimplemented per its published design) as one of several generators in this benchmark study.

paper-intelligent-lost-circulation-monit.summary: This paper proposes an intelligent lost circulation monitoring model for deep and offshore drilling that incorporates geological lithology information alongside real-time drilling parameters, comparing ANN, LSTM, and TCN architectures for risk identification. The temporal convolutional network achieves the best accuracy (93.7%), improved further by including lithology and pump on/off information. To address the scarcity of lost-circulation risk samples, the authors apply CTGAN to augment the small-sample training data before model training.

paper-machine-learning-model-heart-2024.summary: This conference paper proposes a heart failure survival prediction pipeline that uses large language model-based data expansion to address small-sample-size limitations, combined with a novel collaborative-filtering feature selection method and a DeepSurv-based survival model, evaluated on a 299-patient dataset. The paper's introduction discusses GAN-based data augmentation approaches in the medical field as related prior work. CTGAN (Xu et al.'s conditional GAN for tabular data) appears only in the reference list as a cited prior method, not run in the reported experiments.
paper-machine-learning-model-heart-2024.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev library, a reimplementation, or merely cited alongside the LLM-based data expansion approach.

paper-machine-learning-techniques-diagri.summary: This paper studies how architectural and structural parameters relate in diagrid tall buildings, using feature selection and data augmentation to work around a small initial dataset, then training ML classifiers to assess design feasibility. To expand the limited dataset, the authors apply the Gaussian copula algorithm from the Synthetic Data Vault library, learning marginal CDFs and correlations to generate new tabular data points tenfold. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer is run directly as the sole data augmentation engine underpinning the entire empirical study.

paper-power-transformer-dga-augmentation.summary: This conference paper addresses class imbalance in dissolved gas analysis (DGA) data used for power transformer fault diagnosis by applying CTGAN to generate synthetic samples for minority fault classes. The authors implement the technique in Python, explicitly installing the 'ctgan' library, and evaluate fidelity of the synthetic data via descriptive statistics and evenness indices compared to real DGA data. CTGAN (the sdv-family conditional tabular GAN) is run as the sole generative model underpinning the entire data augmentation pipeline.
paper-power-transformer-dga-augmentation.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was imported directly or a custom reimplementation was used, so api_user vs port is inferred from the description of CTGAN as 'proposed' rather than reimplemented.

paper-predicting-masticatory-muscle-acti.summary: This clinical study collected electrognathography, electromyography, and joint vibration data from 66 participants to build predictive models of masticatory muscle activity and jaw deviation during mouth opening, using XGBoost and other machine-learning models evaluated by RMSE and MAE. Because the underlying human sample was small, the authors trained their predictive models on synthetic observations expanded from the 66 real observations, citing the Synthetic Data Vault paper as the basis for this synthetic data generation step. SDV is used to generate the augmented training data underlying the entire predictive modelling pipeline, though the specific synthesizer or algorithm invoked is not stated in the available evidence.
paper-predicting-masticatory-muscle-acti.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV software was directly run (api_user) or only cited for the synthetic-data concept, nor which specific synthesizer/algorithm was used to expand the 66-observation dataset.

paper-synthesizing-realistic-gans-balanc.summary: This is a comparative survey and small experimental study of GAN-based tabular synthetic-data generators (MedGAN, TableGAN, CTGAN, CW-GAN, PATE-GAN, SDV, FakeDB), evaluating a subset of them on machine-learning utility, statistical similarity, and privacy leakage metrics on a shared dataset. SDV is discussed in its own section, described as using Bayesian networks to model dependencies between tables and columns, but it is not included among the four generators actually run in the experiments (MedGAN, CTGAN, TableGAN, CW-GAN). CTGAN is treated as one of several evaluation subjects, with its architecture, training-by-sampling method and mode-specific normalization described at length before being scored in the results tables, while SDV itself is only cited and described, never executed.
paper-synthesizing-realistic-gans-balanc.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN experiments used the actual sdv-dev CTGAN package or the authors' own reimplementation of the architecture they describe in detail (no import/package name or constructor parameters are given); this affects whether integration should be api_user or port.

paper-synthetic-mobility-feature-generat.summary: This paper proposes a diffusion-model-based pipeline for augmenting limited human-mobility feature datasets: mobility features are transformed into images via UMAP, a diffusion model generates new images, and these are converted back into mobility features to improve mental-health state prediction from wearable/GPS data. Evaluated on data from 8 nurses with QIDS depression scores, the method improves accuracy, precision, recall, and specificity over traditional approaches. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing, grouped with other deep-learning synthetic data generation methods (GAN/VAE/diffusion) in a background citation list, with no experimental engagement.
paper-synthetic-mobility-feature-generat.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is discussed beyond the citation list or used as an experimental baseline.

paper-accurate-classification-major-brai.summary: This paper presents NuCLear, a method combining in vivo two-photon imaging of histone 2B-eGFP-labeled cell nuclei with deep learning to classify major brain cell types and their 3D spatial distribution in the mouse cortex over time. To balance the number of training examples across cell types and avoid classification bias, the authors generated synthetic nuclei-feature datasets using the SDV package, which models correlations between features along with summary statistics. The Synthetic Data Vault is run as a component of the training pipeline to produce class-balancing synthetic data for the neural network classifier.

paper-application-fuzzy-logic-detection-.summary: This paper proposes a fuzzy-logic rule system, built via multi-subject multicriteria expertise, to detect financial and customs violations, testing the system on synthetic data generated with the Gretel online platform before validating on real Customs Agency data. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only as background support for the claim that a large share of AI training data is now synthetically generated, and no SDV code, model, or output is used anywhere in the work.
paper-application-fuzzy-logic-detection-.needs: Full text not available; unable to confirm whether SDV is mentioned elsewhere beyond this generic citation.

paper-developing-synthetic-datasets-reef.summary: This conference paper presents a synthetic data pipeline built for the ADRIA (Adaptive Dynamic Reef Intervention Algorithm) reef decision-support model, generating tabular reef-composition data, temporal wave/heat-stress data, and spatial larval-connectivity data without revealing sensitive Great Barrier Reef site information. The pipeline uses conditional sampling methods to preserve spatial relationships across the synthetic datasets for publication, model testing, and method validation. It explicitly draws on methods from the Python package Synthetic Data Vault (Patki, Wedge & Veeramachaneni 2016) alongside other techniques to build this pipeline.

paper-leveraging-synthetic-bias-mitigati.summary: This paper proposes Fair-GAN, a bias-mitigation technique that replaces the SMOTE-based Fair-SMOTE approach with GAN-based synthetic data generation to correct class and demographic imbalances tied to protected attributes such as race and gender. The method is evaluated on benchmark fairness problems using metrics like statistical parity difference and disparate impact. The Synthetic Data Vault's CTGAN and TVAE models are run directly, with default parameters, as the synthetic data generators underlying the whole experimental evaluation.
paper-leveraging-synthetic-bias-mitigati.needs: Full text not obtained; industry domain and any specific benchmark datasets used could not be confirmed beyond the abstract's general framing.

paper-applying-generative-model-improve-.summary: This conference paper addresses reducing the number of TFT current-voltage (IV) measurement points needed for AMOLED display characterization, using an asymmetric autoencoder to reconstruct IV curves from sparse samples and a distilled GPT-2 model trained on encoded IV text to generate synthetic data for rare abnormal cases. The described generative pipeline is built around language-model-based text generation rather than tabular synthesis. The SDV paper is cited but no SDV component, model, or code is described as being run in the abstract or citing sentence.
paper-applying-generative-model-improve-.needs: No full text or citing sentence was available; cannot confirm whether SDV is engaged with beyond an undifferentiated citation.

paper-comparative-analysis-machine-learn.summary: This conference paper surveys and compares the architectures of various GAN models (including basic GAN, CGAN, WGAN and others) used for generating synthetic credit card transaction data to address class imbalance in fraud detection. It is a comparative/review study rather than a novel model or empirical benchmark, discussing the evolution of GAN architectures. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni) is cited only in the reference list as prior work on synthesizing tabular data with GANs, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the body text.
paper-comparative-analysis-machine-learn.needs: Full text not obtained; abstract suggests a comparative survey of GAN architectures for fraud detection but it is unclear whether TGAN itself is among the models actually implemented/benchmarked or only cited for background concept.

paper-balancing-hyper-parameter-optimiza.summary: This paper proposes a framework for IoT network intrusion detection that applies data pre-processing, including class balancing, alongside hyper-parameter optimization (TPE, BOHB, PSO) to tune random forest, gradient boosting, and deep neural network classifiers on the BoT-IoT and ToN-IoT datasets. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing, in a related-work sentence noting that it and ACGAN allow conditional sampling from a specific attack type after training on the whole dataset, but neither model is implemented or evaluated in the study.
paper-balancing-hyper-parameter-optimiza.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is actually implemented/run in the proposed data-balancing pipeline or only cited as related work.

paper-enabling-synthetic-adoption-regula.summary: Proposes DAISYnt, a comprehensive test suite cataloguing statistical similarity, data utility and privacy metrics to evaluate synthetic tabular data quality, applied to real-world Credit Bureau data. Multiple generative models are trained and the best replica is selected using DAISYnt's metrics. SDV's out-of-the-box Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, CopulaGAN and TVAE models are run unmodified as the generative algorithms whose synthetic output the entire empirical evaluation is built on.

paper-noleaks-differentially-private-cau.summary: This paper proposes NOLEAKS, a differentially private causal discovery algorithm for functional causal models that uses a quasi-Newton optimization approach to achieve high accuracy and efficiency, evaluated on public benchmarks and synthetic data against prior private causal discovery methods like EM-PC and Priv-PC. The SDV dissertation is only listed in the reference list and is not discussed or used anywhere in the body text.
paper-noleaks-differentially-private-cau.needs: No citing sentence or full text was available; cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed, used as a data source, or merely listed in related work.

paper-synthetic-generation-comparative-2.summary: This paper compares several generative approaches for tabular synthetic data—GAN, VAE, SMOTE, DataSynthesizer, SynthPop, and two SDV-family methods (Gaussian Copula and a conditional GAN)—across multiple datasets, evaluating them with pairwise correlation and SD metrics and comparing processing time. SDV's Gaussian Copula model (SDV-G) and its conditional GAN (SDV-GAN) are run as two of the several generators under comparison, and SDMetrics is used to compute the SD utility metrics for all models.
paper-synthetic-generation-comparative-2.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV-GAN was run via the sdv library's CTGAN implementation or a separate reimplementation, nor obtain author affiliations.

paper-synthetic-patient-generation-evalu.summary: This paper develops a framework that applies synthetic data generation to eight small, imbalanced medical tabular datasets, evaluating statistical fidelity with three metrics and downstream classification performance (F1-score) across four ML classifiers trained on real, synthetic, and combined data. Two generation algorithms were run directly on each dataset with default hyperparameters: a statistical Gaussian Copula and a deep-learning Conditional Tabular GAN, comparing their behavior on data-integrity preservation and classification utility. CTGAN is run as one of the two generators underpinning the entire empirical programme, including its conditional generation mechanism used to balance case/control samples, while Gaussian Copula (also part of the SDV family) is run as the comparison method.
paper-synthetic-patient-generation-evalu.needs: Reference [18] for Gaussian Copula is not confirmed in the given metadata as an SDV-family citation (only ctgan-neurips-2019 is listed), so its inclusion as an SDV component is inferred from context rather than confirmed citation.

paper-boosting-synthetic-generation-effe.summary: This paper proposes GENCDA, a synthetic tabular data generator that discovers nonlinear causal relationships among variables by restricting an expensive causal-discovery algorithm to features found via frequent pattern mining, then uses these causal relationships at generation time. The method is validated on synthetic datasets with known ground-truth DAGs and on real datasets, comparing accuracy, error, and outlier measures against a random baseline and against SDV's TVAE and CTGAN generators. SDV's TVAE and CTGAN are run with default parameters as two of several comparison generators against which GENCDA's synthetic data quality and runtime are benchmarked.

paper-reply-rc3-2021.summary: This paper investigates whether copula-based statistical models (Gaussian, vine-parametric, vine-nonparametric) can generate synthetic training data to improve machine-learning emulators of physical processes, testing the approach on a toy model of downwelling longwave radiation. The authors find that copula-augmented training sets reduce mean absolute error by up to 62% relative to a non-augmented baseline. SDV's founding paper (Patki et al., 2016) is cited as prior evidence that copula-based models can generate synthetic data comparable to real data, particularly in privacy-protection contexts, but SDV itself is not run; the authors implement their own copula models for the weather/climate application.
paper-reply-rc3-2021.needs: Metadata lists this record's type as 'peer-review' with title 'Reply on RC3', but the supplied full text is the published GMD paper itself ('Copula-based synthetic data augmentation for machine-learning emulators'); the paper title was taken from the full text rather than the metadata title.

paper-lstm-bat-rusboost-electricity-2020.summary: This paper proposes an electricity theft detection system for smart meters that combines LSTM-based feature extraction with a bat-algorithm-tuned RUSBoost classifier to address class imbalance, overfitting, and high-dimensional time-series data, showing improved F1-score and ROC performance over SVM, CNN, and logistic regression baselines. The CTGAN paper is cited only as the source of a normalization equation and appears unconnected to any actual use of the CTGAN model or its methodology.
paper-lstm-bat-rusboost-electricity-2020.needs: The citation appears to be a mis-citation/misattribution; CTGAN's actual method is never engaged with.

paper-machine-learning-techniques-analyz.summary: This paper studies historical labeled airline disruption data from a Mexico-based carrier, using Jeppesen's recovery solver context to predict whether an operator will use manual solutions or the automated recovery solver, comparing neural network and boosting models. The SDV paper is cited only as background evidence for the growing need for synthetic data in machine learning, with no SDV code or method used in the study.

paper-supporting-database-constraints-sy.summary: This SIGMOD student-abstract paper extends the TGAN algorithm to enforce database constraints during synthetic relational data generation, adding a penalty term to the GAN loss so generated tuples satisfy user-specified atomic constraints. The authors implement and experimentally compare several constraint-aware extensions of TGAN. In their related-work discussion they describe the Synthetic Data Vault as a classical-statistics approach that uses the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to select column distributions, but it is only cited, not run.
paper-supporting-database-constraints-sy.needs: The empirical work centers on extending TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018), a distinct citation from the SDV DSAA-2016 paper; the SDV mention is descriptive related-work only.

paper-working-deep-generative-models-202.summary: This conference paper investigates the use of deep generative models (GANs and VAEs) for imputing missing values in tabular data, arguing that prior comparisons in this space suffer from ambiguous dataset naming, unclear hyperparameter tuning, and inconsistent evaluation metrics. It surveys existing generative approaches to motivate a fairer benchmarking methodology for imputation methods. TGAN is cited and described in related work for its recurrent-network-based approach to generating mixed numerical and categorical tabular data, but there is no evidence it was run in the experiments.
paper-working-deep-generative-models-202.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was actually run in the imputation experiments or only described in related work.

paper-utility-synthetic-2019.summary: This paper empirically evaluates the utility of synthetic tabular data by comparing two publicly available synthesis approaches, the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) and DataSynthesizer, across several datasets and supervised ML tasks (classification accuracy, F1 score, and distance-to-original measures). The authors run SDV's default Gaussian Copula model to generate synthetic training data and compare downstream model performance and privacy-related distance metrics against DataSynthesizer with and without differential privacy. SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer is run directly as one of two generators under evaluation, forming a core part of the empirical comparison.
paper-utility-synthetic-2019.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV/HMA was actually run as one of the evaluated generators or only cited as related work in the survey portion.

paper-synthetic-test-generation-recurren.summary: A position paper from an industrial-academic team investigating recurrent neural networks for generating synthetic test data to populate production-like test environments while respecting privacy constraints, motivated by a case study with Norway's National Registry. The authors survey prior synthetic data generation approaches, including probabilistic relational models and RNN-based methods, and report preliminary experiments generating representative data with an RNN. SDV is cited in the related-work discussion as a general end-to-end synthetic data generator that synthesizes complete relational database tables while preserving statistical and structural resemblance to the original data.
paper-synthetic-test-generation-recurren.needs: Whether the relational_hma concept tag is warranted given the paper describes SDV's multi-table synthesis functionality without naming HMA explicitly.

paper-sdv-dsaa-2016.summary: The founding SDV paper. Introduces generative modeling of an entire multi-table relational database via recursive conditional parameter aggregation, and evaluates it by having data scientists solve predictive tasks on synthetic versus real data with no statistically significant difference in outcome.

preprint-inference-time-refinement-close.summary: This paper introduces TARDIS, an inference-time refinement framework for tabular diffusion models that steers and post-hoc filters a frozen pre-trained backbone (e.g. TabDiff) toward the real-data manifold via a Bidirectional Chamfer Refinement pattern, achieving downstream-utility gains over real-data training and over the diffusion backbone across 15 benchmarks. CTGAN is cited only in the related-work survey of tabular generative models as a GAN-based approach using conditional sampling and mode-specific normalization, and is not run or benchmarked in the experiments.
preprint-inference-time-refinement-close.needs: The appendix also cites TVAE under the same reference number [24] (likely a mis-citation in the extracted text) and discusses whether TVAE/TabularARGN could be used as backbones for Stage III; it is unclear from available excerpts whether TVAE was actually run in Table 3's backbone comparison.

preprint-synthesizing-diverse-network-fl.summary: This paper presents a scalable machine-learning pipeline for generating synthetic dynamic multigraph network-flow (netflow) datasets, combining a stochastic Kronecker graph generator for topology, a tabular GAN for edge features, and an XGBoost model for graph alignment, with new metrics to evaluate accuracy and diversity of synthetic graphs versus prior large-scale graph generation methods. CTGAN is used as the feature-generation stage, trained to learn edge-feature distributions with mode-specific normalization applied to continuous values and one-hot encoding for discrete ones, and sampled to produce synthetic netflow features overlaid onto the generated graph structure.
preprint-synthesizing-diverse-network-fl.needs: Not clear whether the sdv-dev/ctgan package was actually run or the authors reimplemented CTGAN themselves; no library name, import, or hyperparameter names are given, so integration mechanism (api_user vs port) is ambiguous.

preprint-primer-synthetic-health-2024.summary: A narrative review/primer mapping the landscape of synthetic health data, covering generation and evaluation methods, tools, deployment examples, regulatory and governance issues, and future opportunities for the health data field. It surveys existing toolkits, describing SDV as a flexible, well-documented Python platform offering copula-based and CTGAN-based synthesis plus emerging SDMetrics evaluation and SDGym benchmarking, while noting its non-commercial license restrictions. SDV, CTGAN, SDMetrics and SDGym are described in prose as part of the synthetic-data tooling landscape but are not run or benchmarked by the authors themselves.
preprint-primer-synthetic-health-2024.needs: Aalborg University Hospital's affiliation_type classification (academic vs government) is uncertain from evidence; treated as academic given pairing with Aalborg University.

preprint-adaptive-robust-watermark-gener.summary: This paper proposes a theoretically grounded watermarking algorithm for generative tabular data, providing guarantees on fidelity, detectability, robustness, and hardness of decoding, and validating them on synthetic and real-world tabular datasets. To produce the synthetic data used in its experiments, the authors generate tables with CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian Copula using the default hyperparameters found in the SDV library, and measure downstream machine-learning efficacy (MLE gap) as a fidelity/utility metric. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula synthesizers are run directly via the library as the data-generation backbone underlying the paper's watermarking experiments.

preprint-augmenting-offline-reinforcemen.summary: This preprint proposes DITS, a method that augments offline reinforcement learning by using state-only online interactions: a conditional diffusion model generates high-return trajectories which are then stitched to the original offline data to improve downstream RL. It evaluates the fidelity of generated versus expert data distributions using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and Pearson rank correlation, metrics it attributes to Patki et al. (2016), the original Synthetic Data Vault paper. SDV is cited only as the source of these evaluation metrics, not run as a synthesizer or library in the pipeline.
preprint-augmenting-offline-reinforcemen.needs: SDV is cited only for a metric methodology, not run as software; no sdmetrics library invocation is described.

paper-debiasing-synthetic-dgm-2024.summary: Shows that estimates computed on synthetic tabular data inherit a bias from the generator that ordinary corrections miss, and gives a debiasing strategy that restores root-n convergence of the standard error and returns confidence-interval coverage close to nominal, demonstrated in a simulation study and two clinical case studies. The strategy is generator-agnostic but is developed and evaluated entirely on CTGAN and TVAE, trained at the default hyperparameters of Synthcity in the simulations and of the SDV package in the case studies.

preprint-targeted-synthetic-generation-t.summary: This paper proposes a targeted data-augmentation pipeline for tabular binary classification that first identifies 'hard' training points using KNN data Shapley values, then trains a synthetic data generator only on those hardest points, showing improved out-of-sample performance over non-targeted augmentation on simulated, American Express credit, and UCI datasets. The generators used throughout the experiments are CTGAN and TVAE, implemented via a heavily customized, forked version of the sdv and ctgan Python packages with custom early stopping. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers, run through a modified fork of the sdv/ctgan libraries, form the empirical backbone of the entire targeted-augmentation study.
preprint-targeted-synthetic-generation-t.needs: Whether the fork's 'custom early stopping' modification is substantial enough to count as derivative_work rather than api_user is a judgment call; treated here as api_user since the core CTGAN/TVAE architecture is unmodified.

preprint-timeautodiff-unified-framework-.summary: This paper proposes TimeAutoDiff, a latent-diffusion framework that pairs a lightweight VAE with a diffusion model over the latent space to unify unconditional generation, imputation, forecasting, and metadata-conditional generation for heterogeneous time-series tabular data. It is evaluated against several baseline generators across six real-world datasets using discriminative, temporal-correlation, and predictive metrics. CTGAN is cited only as related prior art for mixed-type tabular GANs, while CPAR, the autoregressive sequential model from SDV's DeepEcho line, is run as one of five baseline models the authors compare TimeAutoDiff against.
preprint-timeautodiff-unified-framework-.needs: Unclear whether CPAR was run via the DeepEcho/SDV package directly or a reimplementation; text says comparisons use 'publicly available codes' but does not confirm the SDV library was invoked.

preprint-scoping-review-privacy-utility-.summary: This is a PRISMA-ScR scoping review of 92 studies that builds an ontology of methods used to evaluate the privacy and utility of synthetic health-related data, finding wide inconsistency in utility metrics and a general failure to properly assess privacy risk. Synthetic Data Vault is mentioned in passing as one of several open-source platforms (alongside Table Evaluator and TAPAS) built to help researchers create and measure synthetic data quality, and SDV's CopulaGAN synthesizer appears as one of the generative methods identified among the surveyed literature's own tools, without being run by the review's authors.
preprint-scoping-review-privacy-utility-.needs: The review does not run SDV itself; CopulaGAN's appearance reflects tallying of the surveyed literature's tool usage, not the authors' own experiments.

preprint-ffpdg-fast-fair-private-2023.summary: This preprint proposes FFPDG, a fast, fair and private synthetic data generation method for supervised/unsupervised learning that avoids the high computation and bias issues of GAN-based approaches, validated theoretically and on COMPAS and Adult datasets. The authors compare FFPDG's speed and fairness against several private/fair generation baselines, including CTGAN and Copula GAN evaluated on the Adult dataset, and list the Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al. 2016) among the code used. SDV's CopulaGAN and CTGAN synthesizers are run as comparison baselines to test whether the paper's fairness/predictability findings generalize to other generation techniques.
preprint-ffpdg-fast-fair-private-2023.needs: Not fully clear whether the CTGAN/CopulaGAN runs used the sdv-dev package directly or an independent implementation; the 'Code we used' citation to Patki et al. 2016 suggests the SDV library but no explicit import or parameter list is shown.

preprint-improving-irregular-temporal-mo.summary: This retrospective cohort study augments an ICU medication dataset with synthetic data to improve prediction of fluid overload, comparing SMOTE-augmented, CTGAN-augmented, and combined training scenarios across four machine-learning algorithms plus a stacking meta-learner. The best-performing model, a meta-learner trained on the original plus SMOTE plus CTGAN data, achieved 0.83 AUROC with improved sensitivity for the minority class. The authors state their CTGAN model 'was developed with previously proposed architecture [31]', i.e., they reimplemented CTGAN's conditional generative architecture themselves rather than running the sdv-dev package, using it as one of two synthetic data generators whose output is central to the study's headline results.
preprint-improving-irregular-temporal-mo.needs: Reference [31] appears to be the original CTGAN paper; the authors describe reimplementing the architecture rather than citing use of the sdv-dev/ctgan package, so this is judged as a reimplementation (port) rather than api_user.

preprint-lucid-gan-conditional-generativ.summary: This paper proposes LUCID-GAN, a bias-detection method that generates canonical inputs revealing a black-box model's desired feature values for a given prediction, replacing the gradient-based inverse design of the earlier LUCID method with a conditional generative model. It is evaluated on the UCI Adult and COMPAS datasets to expose proxy and intersectional discrimination without needing access to training data. LUCID-GAN is built directly on CTGAN, extending its conditional vector to incorporate the black-box model's predictions while reusing CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and hyperparameter defaults.

preprint-language-models-realistic-tabul.summary: This paper proposes GReaT, an auto-regressive large-language-model-based method that generates realistic synthetic tabular data by learning textual encodings of table rows and supports conditioning on arbitrary feature subsets. It benchmarks GReaT against CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN across multiple real-world tabular datasets using measures of data quality, discriminative similarity, and machine-learning efficacy. SDV's CopulaGAN, CTGAN, and TVAE are run unmodified as baseline generators throughout the paper's empirical evaluation, with GReaT shown to outperform them on most datasets.

preprint-marginal-tail-adaptive-normaliz.summary: This machine-learning paper extends normalizing flows to correctly capture heavy-tailed marginal distributions, proving that autoregressive flows with mixed heavy/light-tailed marginals require a new base-distribution design, and introduces a marginal tail-adaptive flow (mTAF) built on data-driven linear layers. In synthetic experiments the authors fit a Gaussian copula as one comparison baseline using the copulas library's default settings. The SDV-family copulas package's Gaussian copula model is run, unmodified, as one of several baselines against the proposed flow.
preprint-marginal-tail-adaptive-normaliz.needs: Affiliation mapping between the two numeric superscripts and 'Center of Computer Science' vs 'Ruhr University Bochum' is inferred from the byline layout, not fully disambiguated.

preprint-synthetic-what-why-how-2022.summary: A non-technical explainer report commissioned by the Royal Society, surveying the landscape of synthetic data technologies with a focus on privacy, fairness, and data augmentation applications, and outlining risks and evaluation challenges. It reviews prior work broadly, including a taxonomy figure listing SDV alongside other tabular/GAN-based generators and citing SDV's crowdsourced evaluation study and its use of Gaussian copulas. SDV is only cited and diagrammed as one of many named prior methods, never run or evaluated empirically.

preprint-goal-feasibility-diversity-orie.summary: This paper proposes a Deep Generative Model for engineering design that jointly optimizes for performance, feasibility, diversity, and target achievement via a differentiable Design Target Achievement Index loss, tested on a multi-objective bicycle frame design problem. It benchmarks the proposed model against several other generative approaches including a vanilla GAN and MO-PaDGAN. CTGAN, the Conditional Tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run unmodified as one of several baseline generators to which the proposed method is compared.

preprint-generative-quantum-learning-joi.summary: This physics preprint develops a quantum machine learning framework ('qopula') that maps copulas to maximally entangled quantum states, then trains a quantum GAN and a quantum circuit Born machine to learn joint distributions from stock-market data on IonQ trapped-ion hardware. The authors argue for exponential expressivity advantages over classical copula-based generative models and validate against classical GAN baselines. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in a reference-list grouping on copula-based generative modeling, alongside vine copula autoencoders, with no indication that SDV software was run.

preprint-tablegan-mca-evaluating-members.summary: This paper proposes TableGAN-MCA, a membership collision attack that recovers partial training data of a GAN-based tabular data generator from only synthetic samples released by a black-box model. The authors evaluate the attack against four generative models (CTGAN, TVAE, WGAN-GP, WGAN-WC) trained on three real-world datasets, measuring both synthetic data utility and attack success, and also test differential-privacy mitigations. CTGAN and TVAE are implemented by directly using the CTGANSynthesizer and TVAESynthesizer modules from SDGym, making them two of the four target/victim generative models whose synthetic data is attacked and analyzed throughout the empirical study.

paper-patient-level-open-science-2020.summary: Asks whether patient-level data can be published for open science without compromising confidentiality, and evaluates five synthesis methods against that bar. CTGAN produces the structured tabular arm, an early appearance of the architecture in the open-science framing rather than the machine-learning one.

repo-youtube-tutorials.summary: Companion code for a Python tutorial channel, one directory per video topic. The synthetic-data episode is built on SDV: `SingleTableMetadata` and `CTGANSynthesizer` are the whole of the notebook, making this a teaching artifact for the single-table API.
